newsitem.title: Australia: RTRS-Australian stocks close sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks close sharply lower.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2345 -49 US 30yr cl 6.85 +0.02
*Stocks end lower as profit-takers cash in Wall St fall.
Options drove turnover. Volume 452.6 million shares, value A$1.51
bln, 1,083 stocks traded, 298 steady, 286 rises, 499 falls
Australian shares closed sharply lower on Friday as profit-taking erased all of Thursday's record-breaking gains following another fall on Wall Street.
Options exercises, following Thursday's October series expiries, drove volumes and the vast majority of turnover put through the market was before the start of trade.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index ended 42.4 points lower at 2,335.2, it biggest one day fall since July 16.
The December share price index slumped 49 points to 2,345, at a 9.8 point premium to the underlying index.

Stuart Smith, senior dealer at Brisbane broker Lance Jones, said he believed the sharpness of the fall reflected the market's disappointment that the Reserve Bank did not move to lower rates this morning.
"Basically there was too much euphoric buying yesterday on comments from the prime minister that the wages data would prompt a rate cut," Stuart said.

Dealer said falls were across the board although blue chip issues bore the brunt of selling activity especially the big resource issues CRA, WMC and BHP following their steady rises earlier this week.

One of the few bright areas for the market was the wine sector with a number of the small capitalised wineries forging ahead after Brian McGuigan Wines reported strong first quarter earnings on Thursday.
In other local markets, Australian bonds and bill futures ended weaker on profit-taking following the market's strong rally earlier in the week.
The yield on 10 year T-bonds closed at 7.42 percent, up 0.05 percentage points from Thursday's closing level.

The Australian dollar was slightly stronger in late afternoon trade after garnering strength from the Reserve Bank's inaction on interest rates this morning. At 4.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7936/41.

FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade quietened dramatically after Thursday's expiries while futures business picked up due to the market turn around and the big physical volume created by Thursday's option expiries.
